messages:
anita.sre: ok team, after yesterday's page I sketched a small proposal for improving our post-incident followup workflow. main goals: speed up scheduling, make action items visible in one place, and reduce manual bookkeeping. thoughts?

matt.engoncall: yes please. the current slack thread + google doc combo is getting messy. busy oncall cycles mean a lot of actions slip.

sam.pm: +1. we also need a compact customer-impact field in the PM template so we can prioritize remediation by user-facing risk.

olive.reliability: can we automate extracting who was paged and which runbooks were attempted? that would help triage gaps.

anita.sre: exactly — proposal sketch:
- incident bot (incbot) creates a postmortem stub when an incident is marked resolved. stub includes: incident id, severity, who was paged, callouts for customer-facing incidents, and links to logs/traces.
- the bot opens a lightweight follow-up thread with scheduling options for the postmortem (2x time slots with a quick reaction-based RSVP).
- all action items go into a remediation dashboard (table) with owner, due-date, severity, and a small status enum (open/in-progress/blocked/done).

matt.engoncall: reaction-based RSVP is great — less friction. also add automatic reminders (7d, 30d) for overdue actions.

irene.ops: we should capture whether the incident triggered an oncall handoff. those handoffs need a flag in the postmortem so we can review handoff quality separately.

anita.sre: agreed. sample incbot payload I was thinking of (YAML):
```yaml
incident_id: INC-2026-0422
severity: Sev2
paged_teams:
  - eng-oncall
  - eng-runtime
runbooks_attempted:
  - runtime/kv-cache-restart
customer_impact: "partial degradation: 12% requests 500s over 12m"
postmortem_suggestions:
  - proposed_slots:
      - "2026-04-23T15:00Z"
      - "2026-04-24T09:00Z"
  - auto_create_stub: true
action_template:
  - description: "Investigate root cause of cache eviction pattern"
    owner: "<assignable>"
    priority: high
    due_days: 14
```

sam.pm: love the customer_impact line. can the bot populate a tl;dr that we can paste into customer comms?

incbot: @channel postmortem stub created for INC-2026-0422 — actions: 2 assigned, 1 unassigned. React with :calendar: to pick a postmortem slot. More details: <link-to-stub>

olive.reliability: small UX ask — let the RSVP reactions be mapped to a calendar invite we can accept/decline. no copying into gcal every time.

anita.sre: yep, automation should push an invite once a slot reaches >=3 attendees. fallback: PM creates invite if less than 3 after 24h.

matt.engoncall: on the remediation dashboard: we should expose filters — by incident, by owner, by SLA impact. also a quick export to csv for exec reporting.

irene.ops: and include a "customer priority" tag (prod-mission-critical / revenue-impact / internal-only). that will make follow-ups triageable across teams.

sam.pm: can we add a small QA step: when an action is marked done, incbot pings the postmortem author to verify resolution matches the intended remediation? avoids sloppy closes.

anita.sre: good call. also add an automatic postmortem template with fields: summary, timeline, detection, mitigation, root cause hypothesis, root cause analysis (link to logs), customer impact, follow-ups (table). minimal required fields for publishing.

matt.engoncall: implementation note: prefer incremental rollout. 1) incbot creates stub + action items automatically. 2) add RSVP + invite integration. 3) surface actions in dashboard with filters. 4) add reminders/verify close flows.

olive.reliability: any preference for tech stack for the dashboard? simple is best — a small service + a DB and an embeddable UI. we can start with a shared google sheet as a PoC, but we should design APIs from day 1.

anita.sre: agree. PoC: google sheet + incbot webhooks to append rows. long-term: internal service (graphql) + UI in console.

sam.pm: timeline: PoC in 2 weeks, beta for 1 team in 6 weeks?

matt.engoncall: sounds reasonable. volunteers to drive PoC?

anita.sre: I can own the incbot changes for stub creation + RSVP. matt can own calendar integration and reminders. olive will prototype dashboard. sam will draft the customer impact TL;DR template. irene will own handoff flagging + metrics.

matt.engoncall: happy to take calendar/reminder work.

irene.ops: I'll add a short rubric for handoff quality (3 checkboxes) to the postmortem template.

incbot: created action item 1: "Investigate cache eviction pattern" assigned to matt.engoncall, due 2026-05-06. created action item 2: "Add handoff rubric to postmortem template" unassigned.

anita.sre: ok next steps: I'll open a tiny github repo for the incbot stub code, and a google sheet prototype. I'll post links here in 24h. can people react with :thumbsup: if they agree with scope and owners?

matt.engoncall: :thumbsup: 

olive.reliability: :thumbsup: 

sam.pm: :thumbsup: 

irene.ops: :thumbsup: 

anita.sre: thanks all. let's keep the bar low for the PoC, but collect feedback from oncall rotations so we iterate quickly.

matt.engoncall: one more thought — add a small "training" flag so we can catch incidents caused by operator unfamiliarity and route them to devex for a short doc/update.

anita.sre: added. incbot will add a "training_required" boolean if runbooks were invoked and no one closed the loop with a doc link.

sam.pm: perfect. this will help reduce repeat ops errors.

anita.sre: closing — I'll upload the repo link and sheet later today.

incbot: note: postmortem stub "INC-2026-0422" will auto-escalate open actions after 30d unless flagged with a business reason.
